title: Cost-aware Canary Budgeting Journey
creator: Riley Chen
description: Design a compact, cost-aware canary composer that surfaces estimated spend, unit economics, and guardrail recommendations while teams configure traffic ramps and rollbacks. Goal is to reduce surprises from canaries that spike cost and to provide clear trade-offs between speed of exposure and budget consumption. This ticket covers the user journey, low-fidelity flows, a clickable prototype, and a plan for a lightweight moderated usability study.
background: Product and Growth teams reported several incidents where canary traffic ramps unintentionally increased token costs by 2x for high-traffic routes. Engineering has a new cost-estimation API (ENG-4120) that returns per-route cost projections for candidate traffic splits. Design needs to integrate that data into the rollout composer with minimal friction for engineers and PMs.
goals: Make per-step cost impact visible during canary setup
Provide default budget-safe templates and a budget slider that auto-adjusts ramp schedules
Surface rollback triggers tied to cost anomalies alongside quality signals
Keep the composer compact enough for repeatable use by platform teams
acceptance_criteria: Prototype shows live cost preview for each ramp stage based on sample traffic and model profile
Users can set a total canary budget and see an estimated completion time and exposure profile
Composer suggests a 'cost-sparing' ramp template and explains trade-offs in one line
Usability test (n=6) shows participants can configure a budgeted canary in under 5 minutes with no assistance
Design handoff includes component specs, motion tokens for budget warnings, and an integration spec for the cost API
decisions: Show cost as both absolute monthly estimate and relative percentage vs baseline route
Use a compact horizontal timeline with inline budget chips rather than a full-page wizard
Default to conservative ramp template for new canaries and provide an expert toggle
Rollback policy cards will include cost thresholds alongside latency/error thresholds

ux_notes: Budget slider uses three modes: conservative, balanced, aggressive. Selecting a mode updates ramp percentages and estimated spend.
Inline chips show per-stage estimated tokens and $ cost with a subtle red glow if a stage exceeds the selected budget allocation.
A single-line summary card at the top explains expected cost impact and recommended mitigations (cache warmup, KV prefixing, throttled sampling).
On hover, each stage expands to show sample traffic assumptions and confidence band pulled from ENG-4120
